standard.title: Combine elements to communicate
standard.description: explore ways to combine the elements of drama to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning in improvisations, devised drama and/or scripted drama
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use elements of drama — voice, movement, language, space — in combination to develop dramatic action in improvisations and devised drama (Y3-4). They can make deliberate element choices and describe their effect.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore ways to combine elements of drama to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning in improvisations, devised drama and/or scripted drama.

nodes.label: Using empathy and perspective to develop combination choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use empathy to explore how combining elements differently communicates different perspectives and challenges stereotypes.
nodes.minimum_width: Student makes at least one element combination choice that is informed by a character perspective other than their own default.
nodes.typical_width: Students experiment with empathy when combining elements in improvised and scripted drama; they consider situations from multiple characters' perspectives; they use Viewpoints to explore how cultures shape element use ('How are relationships, language and symbols shaped by cultures?').
wider: Students imagine themselves in the time/place of a historical event, considering why participants made particular decisions, and explore this through deliberate element combinations
Students explore how the same dramatic situation produces different element-combination choices for characters from different cultural backgrounds
nodes.hinge_reason: Empathy-informed element choice is what distinguishes purposeful dramatic crafting from mechanical application of techniques; without this, combinations may be technically correct but lack communicative power — particularly critical in scripted drama where character interior is essential.

response_modes.reason: Use structured empathy activities before script or devising work — 'hot-seating', role-on-the-wall, or perspective-taking exercises — to give students the interior perspective that informs element choices.

success_criteria: Student makes at least one element combination choice informed by a specific character perspective
Student can explain how their combination choice communicates that character's viewpoint or intention

nodes.label: Combining elements across forms — improvised, devised and scripted
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can combine elements of drama purposefully across improvised, devised and scripted forms, evaluating which combinations communicate most effectively.
nodes.minimum_width: Student compares how element combinations produce different effects in at least two different dramatic forms.
nodes.typical_width: Students use improvisation or process drama to compare how improvised and scripted drama create characters and action; they explore how elements combine differently across forms; they consider how cultural understandings shape meaning through element combinations.
wider: Students evaluate drama they experience in live performance, identifying specific element combinations, and consider how to apply those techniques in their own work
Students explore drama from another culture or historical period and investigate how element combinations reflect that culture's dramatic conventions

response_modes.reason: Exploring element combinations across multiple forms and cultural contexts builds the flexible, transferable skill of combining intentionally rather than habitually.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of dramatic forms (improvisation, devised, scripted) and cultural contexts in which element combinations operate is broad; students who explore widely develop stronger metacognitive command of their dramatic choices.
success_criteria: Student combines elements of drama purposefully in at least two different forms
Student evaluates the effectiveness of a specific element combination and suggests an alternative
